text.content:
This manual explains how to play Sacadia's Art of War in Foundry VTT with the Sacadia system: how to build a character, take a turn, and what the system does for you automatically. Players can read the first half; GMs should read all of it.

The rulebook is still the authority on the rules. This manual covers how those rules work on the table: which button does what, what gets rolled and applied for you, and what stays in the GM's hands.

What the system does for you

The system automates any rule that is a roll or a number:

  • Rolls. Attacks, damage, Trait Checks, and saves roll with the right trait, Proficiency, advantage, and bonuses already added. Each result card lists every modifier that applied, so nothing is hidden.
  • Resolution. Attacks are compared against the target's defenses on the GM's side. Players see Hit or Miss, never the NPC's numbers.
  • Conditions. Condition levels, their effects, end-of-turn reduction, and the no-stacking rule are all tracked.
  • Your turn. AP, limb exhaustion, reactions, Focus upkeep, usage limits ("once per turn"), and start-of-turn effects are handled as turns change.
  • Abilities. Nearly every profession ability is wired up. Passives adjust your numbers on their own, Boosts ride your next matching action, and reactions appear as buttons when their moment comes.

What stays with the GM

Some things stay with the table on purpose:

  • Movement. Pushes, pulls, charges, and anything else that moves a token on the map are the GM's to apply. The check that decides whether it happens is still rolled for you.
  • Range and reach. The sheet tells you when a target looks out of range, but it never blocks you.
  • Judgment calls. Anything that depends on the fiction, like whether a creature is found, what counts as cover, or whether a spell gets through a Voidsphere.

How warnings work

When something looks wrong (not enough AP, an ability already used this turn, a target out of range, a condition that isn't met), the system asks "Use it anyway?" rather than refusing. The GM can always overrule the automation.

Where things are

  • This manual: the Sacadia User Manual compendium. You can also open it from Game Settings → User Manual, or from any character sheet's header menu (⋮ → Open the User Manual).
  • Compendia: abilities by profession (including the Magus and Witch prestige professions), Lore Abilities, Profession Masteries, Profession Features & Legendary Masteries, Basic Actions & Reactions, and equipment (weapons, armor, shields, adornments, trinkets).
  • Rules version: the system follows Sacadia's Art of War v1.2 and the Prestige Classes addendum (v0.2-3).

Character creation follows the rulebook's six steps: Culture, Heritage, Ancestry, Profession, Talents, and Background. This page covers where each piece goes on the sheet.

1. Identity and profession

Your name goes at the top of the sheet. On the Character tab, under Build, set your level and primary profession with your level in it (and a secondary one if you multiclass). The prestige professions, Magus and Witch, are chosen the same way. Their features follow your level in that profession. The header sums the build up under your name. Your level and profession set these for you:

  • Proficiency and Max AP, from your level.
  • Max Health, from your profession's HP per level. Use Max HP adjustment (Character tab, under Build) for Heritage HP or a rolled difference.
  • Check DC, from your profession's formula.
  • Lore points, from your level and Fate.
  • Move Speed (header): 30ft, adjusted by your abilities, Heavy Armor, a Tower Shield, and Slowed.

Culture, Heritage, Ancestry, and your backstory prompts go on the Character tab too, under Identity and Background.

2. Traits

On the Stats tab, enter your five Traits: Power, Finesse, Courage, Wiles, and Fate. Click a Trait's icon (or its name) to roll a Trait Check with it. Your profession's Trait Expertise is marked there too.

3. Abilities

Open the compendium for your profession and drag the abilities you've learned onto your sheet. The sheet tracks the Combat Skill Points you spend.

  • Level features. Your profession's level features (Flitting Feet, Semper Steady, Slightly Cracked, and so on) and your Level-11 Legendary Mastery are in Profession Features & Legendary Masteries. Add the ones your level grants; they aren't added automatically.
  • Masteries. Your Level-5 Mastery is in Profession Masteries.
  • Basic actions. Kick, Rend Armor, Help, Block, Dodge, Grab, and the four Opportunity Attacks are given to every character automatically.

Some abilities ask you to make a permanent choice, such as a weapon family, a condition, or a limb. That choice appears as a dropdown on the ability's row. Set it once and the ability uses it from then on.

4. Equipment

Drag weapons and armor from the equipment compendia onto your sheet, then use the Inventory tab.

  • Equip what you're wearing and holding. Only equipped armor counts toward your defenses, and only equipped weapons are used for automatic weapon picks.
  • Weapons attack automatically. Adding a weapon gives you a matching attack ability ("Dagger Attack"). A Versatile weapon (one you can throw) also gets a Throw ability at 40ft.
  • Bound weapon. An attack ability can be bound to a particular weapon from the ability's sheet. If you leave it on Auto, it uses your first equipped weapon.
  • Signature. Use the signature toggle to mark your Fatebound divine weapon.
  • Named Weapons (Bladedancer). Open a Versatile weapon's sheet and pick which of your Named Weapon abilities it carries.
  • Item slots (pp.180–181). Every item takes slots in your readied slots (RIS: 5, what you can reach in combat) or your stored slots (SIS: what your bags hold). The tag on each row swaps it and shows its size; the counter at the top shows both. Reaching a stored item in combat asks first. Carrying more than both hold is Overburdened (half speed).

Size, resistances and talents

  • Size and Resistances are on the Character tab, under Build (an NPC's are in its header). Resistances take a list such as physical 2, fire 5, rot immune (types, the groups physical / elemental / mental, or all; a negative number is a vulnerability). They apply when damage of that type lands; armor with a resistance (Corrupted Iron) adds to it.
  • Specializations (Stats tab, under Talents): add a specialized talent, choose its general talent and its ranks. Its dice button rolls that talent with 1X advantage per rank. A talent you don't have rolls at 1X disadvantage and without Proficiency (p.146).
  • Prerequisites are checked when you drag an ability onto your sheet: if one isn't met (a Trait score, a level, an ability, a specialization rank) you get a warning, but the ability is still added.

5. Pools and profession panels

Class pools such as Glory, Savage, Trickshot, Prescient, Call, Arrangement, Trickster, Spell Slots (Magus), and Divine Touch (Witch) appear beside your AP on the Abilities tab, once you have the ability that grants them. They fill to their maximum when you rest. Some professions also get a panel there:

  • Hulinari Warrior: your Form (Pack, Brute, or Swarm). Toggle Beast Form on your token to take that form.
  • Sentinel: your Favored Enemies (and your Bigger Stones picks, if you have that ability).
  • Oracle: your saved Slightly Cracked rolls.

Rolling initiative

Initiative is a Courage or Finesse Check, whichever is better (book p.233). Once the GM has set up a combat, press Initiative at the top of your sheet. If your token isn't in the Combat Tracker yet, this adds it, then rolls. You roll once per combat: pressing it again just tells you your number, and the GM rerolls from the Combat Tracker.

Starting a turn

Turn tracking needs a combat in Foundry's Combat Tracker. When your turn begins, the system:

  • refills your AP and clears your exhausted limbs;
  • refreshes your reaction for the round;
  • applies start-of-turn effects: Hemorrhage damage, the Insane table if you're Insane, auras you started inside, Battle Fatigue if you're Wounded;
  • clears Boosts you armed but didn't use;
  • ends your Focus abilities that you didn't maintain last turn.

When your turn ends, each of your adversarial conditions drops by one level, except Enduring ones.

AP and limbs

Every action costs AP and exhausts one or more limbs (arm, legs, body, mind). If an action needs a limb you've already exhausted, it costs +1 AP. The Abilities tab shows:

  • your AP (the ↺ button resets your turn if you need to fix a mistake);
  • which limbs are exhausted;
  • the actions you've taken this turn, each with an Undo that refunds its AP and limb.

The Basic Actions buttons (Move, 5ft Adjust, Climb, Drop, Hurdle, Disengage, Switch Item, Steady, Hide, Make Trait Check, and so on) spend AP and limbs for actions that aren't abilities.

Using an ability

  1. Target the creature or creatures first (T, or right-click → target).
  2. Click the ability's icon on your sheet. (Clicking its name opens its description.)
  3. Answer any prompts:
    • Advantage: pick Normal, Advantage, or Disadvantage, or enter a level. Conditions, effects, cover, Surrounded, and so on are added on top automatically.
    • A choice the ability needs, such as which defense to boost or which condition to remove.
    • A variable cost, such as how many pool points to spend.
  4. The result posts to chat as a card showing every roll and every modifier that applied.

The sheet warns (and lets you continue) if you're short on AP, the ability is out of its usage limit, its condition isn't met ("only while raging"), or the target is out of range or Hidden.

Boosts

A Boost changes your next matching action. To use one:

  1. Click the Boost's icon (it shows a bolt) to arm it. Armed Boosts are marked Armed and listed in the Armed Boosts tray; click one there to disarm it.
  2. Use the action it applies to. The Boost's effect is included and it's used up.

Only one Boost per action, and none on reactions (book p.236). Exceptions: Boostbuster and Close Quarter allow one on certain reactions, and Boosted Attack / Boost Stack allow two or three on a divine-weapon attack. If more Boosts are armed than the action allows, you choose which to spend. A Boost whose condition isn't met stays armed.

Reactions

You have one reaction per round, shown as pips in the header. Some abilities give you more. When a reaction becomes possible (an ally is hit, an enemy moves next to you, an attack is about to land on you), the system whispers you a reminder or shows buttons on the GM's resolution card. Reaction-tagged abilities spend your reaction when you use them.

Focus

A Focus ability lasts as long as you maintain it, which means using its Focus action again on each of your turns. If you don't, it ends at the start of your next turn, along with anything it created (marks, grants on allies, zones). Going Insane ends all your Focus abilities at once.

Lore abilities

Your Lore points (from level 4, more with Fate 3 and 6) refill on a Long Rest. Every character has Rousing Success; at levels 4, 9, and 13 you add one more from the Lore Abilities compendium (prerequisites such as an ancestry or profession are listed on each).

  • A Lore ability marked L in the book costs only the Lore point: no AP, Boost, Reaction or Focus. Using one spends the point, and warns if you have none left.
  • Lore Boosts (Blasting Strike, The Hunted, Divine Volley …) arm like any Boost but don't count against the one-Boost limit. Their point is spent when they're used.
  • A few are actions or Focus too (Kickbuck, Shockflock, Summon Beasts) and cost AP as well.
  • Oozing Flow shows up as a button on the GM's card when you're hit.
  • Webcraft targets one enemy per Madness you spend, up to your Proficiency. Target the enemies; it spends one Madness each, and its 5M damage uses your Madness from before the spend.
  • The book lets you decide when a Lore use triggers. Use it on the sheet at the moment you want, and ask the GM to apply anything the card can't (Still Up, for example, is used as you would drop below 0 HP).

Usage limits

"Once per turn", "once per quick rest", and "once per combat" are counted for you. Using an ability past its limit asks for confirmation first. A limit "on a single target" (Beastly Presence) is counted per creature: using it on someone new is fine.

Abilities that may target only so many creatures warn when more are targeted.

Resting

Rests are in the header:

  • Short (Quick) Rest: refills pools, clears most conditions, restores one point of Rend to your armor, and offers to spend Health Pools. Oracles with Slightly Cracked roll their saved d3s.
  • Long Rest: full Health, refills Health Pools and Lore, clears all Rend and repairs broken armor.

Attacks

An attack card shows your to-hit roll and damage roll. The GM's side compares the to-hit against the target's defense (PD, TD, MD, or AD) and adds Hit!, Miss, or Critical Hit! to your card. Players never see an NPC's defenses, DR, or Health.

  • Damage is applied according to the world's Combat resolution setting. By default, damage from player characters is applied automatically, and damage to player characters waits for the GM. The GM gets a private note with the numbers, DR, and Apply / No DR / Undo buttons.
  • Criticals happen on your crit range (natural 20, or lower with abilities). Surprised targets are always critically hit, and so are Steadied Opportunity Attacks. The GM applies your crit choice (Maximize, Critical Harm, or a condition) from the private note.
  • On-hit conditions from the attack are offered to the GM to apply. If the target gets to resist ("Finesse check negates"), the target's player gets a Roll Save to Negate button instead.
  • Multi-attacks (Wild Strike, Dagger Threat, Freefire) roll each attack separately against its own target.
  • Courage on weapon attacks (v1.2 p.219): a weapon attack uses Courage instead of its usual trait when your Courage is higher. The card says so.
  • Untrained attacks (p.6): each profession is trained in certain attacks (most in melee or ranged). An attack your professions aren't trained in rolls without your Proficiency, and the card marks it Untrained. The Witch is trained in none.

Trait Checks forced on a target

When your ability makes someone roll a Trait Check, your card has a Roll Save button. The player who controls the target clicks it with their token selected.

  • A condition is checked once per level: trying to give 3 Pin means 3 checks. Each failed check is one level taken (p.258).
  • Advantage adds dice and keeps the best. Disadvantage turns that many checks into automatic failures.
  • Fumble reduces only the first check (p.257).
  • Damage attached to the check applies on a failure. Some abilities deal half damage on a success.
  • Optional spends such as Confidence, Fateful Saves, and Reactive Mind are offered before the roll.

After the roll: reactions to attacks

Some abilities change an attack after it's rolled: Remaneuver, Lucky Strike, Block, Dodge, Please Don't, Sacrifice, Black Rebuke, Checkered Shield, Absorb Attack, Balanced Fare, and others. When one of them could apply, a button for it appears on the GM's resolution card, labelled with who can use it. Clicking it spends the cost and adjusts the result.

Damage, DR and temporary HP

  • DR reduces damage from each hit, but a hit that gets through always deals at least 1 (v1.2 p.192). Some abilities give extra DR against particular attacks, such as attacks on your MD or while you're Surrounded.
  • Shared damage (Sacrifice, Sacrificial Wing, Law of Alliance): DR applies once, to the whole hit, before it's split. The shares don't apply DR again.
  • Damage types (pp.184, 222): weapon damage takes the weapon's type (bludgeoning, slashing, piercing, imbued, all physical); elemental weapons deal their element, and some abilities deal mental damage. The card shows the type, and the target's Resistances for it (or its group, or all) add to its DR. Elemental damage ignores resistance to physical damage.
  • Temporary HP absorbs damage first. It doesn't stack (you keep the higher amount) and it ends when combat ends.
  • Self-damage from your own abilities (Mad Smear, Bloodlet, Stygian Abyss, Clotsnipe, Life Transference) is reduced by Mistletoe and Blood Mastery. Under a Witch's Self Heal it becomes temporary HP instead.

Wounded, Dying and death (p.230)

  • Below 0 HP you are Wounded. At the start of each of your turns you gain a point of Battle Fatigue, which lowers your AP until you rest. With no AP left you fall Unconscious.
  • Attacks against an Unconscious creature always hit unless the attacker rolls a natural 1.
  • At −½ your max HP you die. The token is marked dead.

Adversarial conditions

Adversarial conditions (Pin, Hemorrhage, Panic, Fatigue, Fumble, and so on) have levels. The Stats tab tracks them, and each appears on your token with its level.

  • Giving one: the target rolls one Trait Check per level you try to give, and takes a level for each failure (see Attacks, Checks and Damage).
  • No stacking: a creature that already has a condition can't be given it again unless the ability says it can (p.258). The system enforces this everywhere. When two parts of one action give the same condition (such as Jagged Blade's extra Hemorrhage), they count as one attempt. Abilities that say otherwise (Witch's Finger, Spring's Surge, a Witch's Poured Mold) are allowed through.
  • Conditions you give yourself do stack: Remaneuver's Sting, Predator and Prey's Sting, and the Fatigue from Steed and Rider, Guard Them, Berserker Rage, leaving Insanity, Give of Thyself, and Transmute Trauma all add to the levels you already have.
  • More than 6 levels are kept, but the condition's effects stop increasing at 6.
  • Losing levels: each held condition drops by one at the end of your turn. Enduring conditions don't: Silenced, a condition made Enduring by Balanced Scale, Luckless Hold or Winter Frost, or Pin held by Wrestling Focus. Fumble clears completely at the end of your turn.
  • Shaking one off: click the condition's name on the Stats tab to open the resist dialog. Make Trait Check rolls one check (+1 per extra AP), and each success removes a level. The Incoming mode rolls the checks for levels the GM asks you to resist.
  • Where it came from: each condition remembers who gave it. That's how Hemorrhage from a creature with Mastery of Hemorrhage or Bloodthinner deals bigger dice every turn. Those upgrades are read from the giver when the Hemorrhage deals damage, so a Witch's Bleeding Bane counts only while she holds it.
  • Rests clear most conditions.

Rend and Corroded

  • Rend removes AD, PD, TD, or MD from armor (p.258), never DR. Each level comes off a random point of a random piece of your worn armor or shield, finishing one piece before moving to the next; Rend Armor's choice and Clever Rend's pick go first. The Inventory tab shows each piece's rend, and a piece with nothing left is Broken. A creature wearing no armor, or with none left, can't be rended.
  • A quick rest restores one point; a long rest restores all of it and repairs broken pieces.
  • Corroded gives one level of Rend per level at the start of your turn. Once there's nothing left to rend, all your Corroded turns into Hemorrhage.

Size and physical effects

Each creature has a Size (a character's Character tab, an NPC's header). Against a physical effect (a physical condition, Prone, Dragged, a Kick), the bigger creature rolls its checks with 1X advantage per size step, and the smaller with that much disadvantage, up to 3 (p.225). The save card shows it.

Simple conditions

Simple conditions are on or off. Toggle them from the token HUD:

  • Prone: your attacks at 1× disadvantage. Melee attacks against you get 1× advantage. You can't take reactions (v1.2); using one warns first.
  • Surprised: attacks that hit you are critical hits. It ends when you take damage or at the start of your turn.
  • Blinded, Dragged, Unconscious, Insane, Raging, Steadied, Beast Form, Wounded: as in the book. Many abilities check whether you have these, so keep them accurate.

The battlefield

These conditions describe your surroundings (pp.254–255). The GM usually toggles them:

  • Cover (Half or Full): set it with the Cover dropdown on your Abilities tab. Attacks against you are at 1× or 2× disadvantage.
  • Surrounded: worked out from the tokens around you. Melee attacks against you get 1× advantage.
  • Cornered: all attacks against you get 1× advantage.
  • Obscured: +3 to AD, PD, MD and TD. Dim and Bright light make creatures Obscured.
  • Shadowed: attacks against you are at 1× disadvantage.
  • Height: your attacks get 1× advantage.
  • Hidden: you can't be directly targeted. The system warns anyone who tries. You're revealed when you attack, force a Trait Check on someone, or take damage. Hide Behind Hide sets Hidden for you.

Madness and Insanity (Oracle)

Madness is its own track from 0 to 6, and it does stack. Oracle abilities raise or lower it automatically when used.

  • Reaching 6 makes you Insane. You stay Insane until Madness falls back to 0, and leaving Insanity gives you Fatigue.
  • While Insane, you roll the Insane table at the start of each turn. Its HP loss is applied for you (Heather Root and Writhing Block reduce or cancel it), and the effect is shown on the card.
  • Madness drops by one at the end of your turn unless something holds it (Voices That Shriek, Bloodlet).
  • Slightly Cracked rolls are made at each rest and shown on your sheet. Arm the Slightly Cracked Boost to use one of them in place of a 1D3−1 Madness roll.

Auras that follow you

Some abilities affect everyone near you while you maintain them. These need no setup:

  • Blade Aura: an enemy that starts its turn within 5ft of you (10ft with Bladius, 15ft with Greatius Bladius) gets a Finesse check card, with the damage already rolled.
  • Blackcloud (v1.2): enemies inside your Clouded Foe make Trait Checks at 1× disadvantage.
  • Hallow's Calm / Hallow's Gale (Magus): attacks made inside the aura are at 1× disadvantage (Calm) or advantage (Gale). The aura starts at 5ft and grows 5ft each turn you renew it, up to 5ft × Proficiency. An Oracle starting its turn inside loses (Calm) or gains (Gale) a point of Madness.
  • Aura of the Grotto / Aura of Bane (Witch): within 5ft × ½ Proficiency, your allies roll checks against adversarial conditions at 1× advantage (Grotto), or your enemies at 1× disadvantage (Bane).
  • Tempered Aura (Witch): everyone within it is immune to Panic and Taunt, and loses any they had on entering.
  • Confusion (Magus): no one else within 30ft (60ft with Distant Confusion) can start a new Focus. The sheet warns if they try.
  • Sphere Insanium: at the start of your turn, every enemy within 30ft gains 2 Delirium, with no check.

Placed zones

Some abilities create an area on the map: Stygian Abyss, Draining Aura, Voidsphere, Suppressing Fire, Focal Point, God's Mist, and Pact of the Earth (30ft of difficult terrain around the Magus). To place one:

  1. Use the ability as normal.
  2. When asked, click the map where the zone goes. Press Esc instead to center it on your target, or on yourself if you have no target. God's Mist always centers on you.
  3. The zone appears as a colored area, a Foundry Region.

After that, the zone works on its own:

  • Checks and damage. A creature that enters the zone or starts its turn inside it gets the zone's check card or damage, at most once per turn.
  • Statuses. Everyone inside Stygian Abyss is Shadowed; you and your allies inside God's Mist are Obscured. These are added and removed as creatures move in and out.
  • Attacks and terrain. Attacks made from inside Suppressing Fire are at 1× disadvantage. Its area (and Stygian Abyss with Pooled Ink at 3+ Madness) is difficult terrain.
  • Size. Madness-sized zones grow and shrink as your Madness changes. God's Mist moves to you at the start of your turn.
  • Upkeep. Stygian Abyss costs you Proficiency HP on each turn it stands, including the turn you cast it.

Swarm clouds (Hulinari, v1.2)

Clouded Foe and Clouded Ally spread your Swarm over X tiles (X = your Proficiency, +1 with Grey Cloud, +2 with Stormcloud, more with Cloudsurge):

  1. Use the ability. The tiles under your token are picked for you.
  2. Click further tiles, each touching the cloud along an edge (no diagonals), until you have X. Press Esc to stop early.
  3. The cloud moves with your token, keeping its shape. With Rolling Fog, it's laid on your target and follows them instead, and your own Move Speed is 0.

Enemies inside your Clouded Foe count as Surrounded; allies inside your Clouded Ally have Partial Cover. Abilities that say "inside your Cloud" (Birdbite, Delirious Flock, Blackcloud, Birdshield, Guiding Wingbeats, Armor Nics, Sacrificial Wing) read it automatically. Birdbite with nothing targeted attacks every enemy in your Clouded Foe. Sharp Cloud and Dark Cloud ride the cloud while you maintain them.

How long a zone lasts: a Focus zone (Suppressing Fire among them) lasts while you maintain the Focus. A zone from a plain action lasts until the start of your next turn. All zones disappear when combat ends. To move a zone ("move the center 10ft each turn"), the GM drags the Region. Whether you're allowed to place a zone that far away is up to you and the GM.

Most abilities just work once they're on your sheet. These notes cover the ones that need a setting or a habit from you.

Bladedancer

  • Named Weapons: open a Versatile weapon's sheet and choose which Named Weapon ability it carries. You can have up to your Proficiency in named weapons. The Vengeance needs you to choose its enemy from the dropdown on its ability row.
  • Throwing: Versatile weapons come with a Throw ability. With Wild Throws, Wild Strike asks whether you're swinging or throwing. Throws count toward I'll Come Back.
  • Exploding Weapon: throw the named weapon at a target, and everyone else within 5ft of them takes its damage. Throw it with nothing targeted to pick a point on the map instead; everyone within 5ft of the point takes the damage.
  • Arrangements spend Arrangement points. The movement itself is yours to make on the map.

Fatebound

  • Mark your divine weapon with the Signature toggle in your inventory. Divine-weapon abilities and Boosts check for it.
  • Glory is spent from the pool beside your AP.
  • Targeted Foe marks your current target. Abilities that care about your Targeted Foe (Crushing Blow, Imbued Fury) check against that mark.

Hulinari Warrior

  • Set your Form (Pack, Brute, or Swarm) on the Abilities tab. Toggle Beast Form on your token when you shift. Form-specific abilities only work in the right form.
  • Swarm (v1.2): Hovering Foe is gone. Swarm abilities work through your Clouded Foe and Clouded Ally tiles; see Zones and Auras. Swarm points are now Trickster Points. A character built under v1.0 swaps the old Swarm abilities (Hovering Foe, Picking at Armor, Sharpbeak …) for the new ones from the compendium.

Oracle

  • Madness, the Insane table, and Slightly Cracked are covered on the Conditions page.
  • Pull the Strand spends a saved Slightly Cracked roll. You choose + or −, and the GM applies it to the enemy's roll.
  • Soulbinding and A Boiled Leech remember the targets you chose when you cast them.

Sentinel

  • Set your Favored Enemies on the Abilities tab. Abilities that care about favored enemies read the target's creature type.
  • Trickshot points are spent from the pool. Variable spends ask how many.

Soldier

  • Toggle Steadied on your token when you Steady. Many Soldier abilities, Block, Dodge, and Grab depend on it.
  • Calls spend Call points. Their buffs go onto the allies you target.

Thug

  • Berserker Rage starts your rage: you're marked Raging for Proficiency rounds (+1 each with Lengthy Rage and Anger Management), counted down at your turn ends. When it ends you gain ⌈Prof/2⌉ Fatigue after your conditions drop, so you still have all of it at your next turn (with Endurance Mastery, a Power Check card instead). While raging, your first melee attack each turn offers to be the free rage attack (no AP or limbs, no Boost).
  • Pin from Natural Wrestler enables Harm and its Boosts. Wrestling Focus keeps your Pin from dropping at the end of turns.
  • Semper Steady treats you as Steadied while you still have your reaction this round.

Magus (prestige)

  • Spell Slots are your pool (refilled on a quick rest). Scrollwriter, the Unfurlings, Mastery of the Tome, and Mastery of the Mind each add 3. Abilities that say "expend X Spell Slots" ask how many.
  • Your Tome is an ability on your sheet. Use it to open its research record: tick the abilities you've researched (each is a Long Rest Action) and press Record. Adding a Tome ability that isn't recorded shows a warning. Prerequisites such as Astrology[3] are shown as text; checking them is up to you and the GM. The record lives on the Tome, so it travels with it.
  • Contract Tome: choose the defense it raises in the dropdown on its row.
  • Blood for Bane is a Boost to any action that spends a Spell Slot. Roll 6 or more and the slot is refunded.
  • Clotsnipe asks how much extra AP to spend. Target every creature in the line.
  • Save-gated Focus (Bane, Catnap, Crown of Insanity, Enemies Abound, Forbid Hallowing): the targets roll once, when you start it, and only those who fail are affected. Renewing it doesn't ask again (Enemies Abound re-checks, and a success ends it).
  • Law of Alliance: damage to anyone bound is split evenly, and you take the odd points. Death Ward stops the next drop to 0 HP at 1 HP and ends the Focus. Lawful Sanctuary makes anyone attacking the warded creature roll a Wiles Check first; on a failure they pick another target.
  • Checkered Shield and Absorb Attack appear as buttons on the GM's card when you're hit.
  • Summons (Animate Dead and its upgrades) have no stat blocks in the addendum; the GM runs them.

Witch (prestige)

  • Your Promise is an ability on your sheet. Use it to mark it broken, or kept again. While it's broken, your Witch abilities warn before use until you take Atone. With Promise of Nonviolence, attacking or bleeding a creature that isn't on your side asks first and breaks it.
  • Divine Touch is your pool (twice your Proficiency with A Full Well).
  • Ally Focuses (Razorleaf, Shield Transference, Fourleaf Touch, Poured Mold, Bleeding Bane …): target the ally when you start it. Renewing warns if they're more than 5ft away. Options such as the weapon type or the defenses are asked each time you use it.
  • One-shot reactions (Hallowed Touch, Tweak the Heart, Wellspring, Blossom): use them before your ally rolls. They apply to that ally's next temp-HP roll, condition attempt, or ability.
  • Two-target abilities (Olive Branch, Transmute Trauma): target the first creature, then the second. For Transmute Trauma the second rolls.
  • Funnel Energy: target both creatures (or just one, with Given Energy, and you're the other). You roll one Fate check per level of the tired creature's Fatigue, against their own Check DC. Each success removes a level and gives the other creature 1 AP on their next turn.
  • Greater Transference strengthens Shield Transference only on an ally, not on an enemy through Foe Transference.
  • Poured Mold: pick the condition on its row. While you hold it, that condition stacks on your target up to your Proficiency, and it's all removed when the Focus drops.
  • Nettle asks which of the target's conditions to convert and what into.
  • Witch's Presence: pick the condition on its row. Your side is immune while you're on the scene and conscious.
  • Balanced Fare and Harmed Fare appear as buttons on the GM's card after a miss or a hit.

World settings

Game Settings → Configure Settings → Sacadia:

  • Combat resolution
    • Default: damage from player characters applies automatically; damage to player characters waits for your click.
    • Fully automatic: damage applies automatically in both directions.
    • Manual: the system decides hit or miss only; you apply all damage yourself.
  • Condition stacking
    • Book (default): a creature that already has a condition can't be given it again.
    • Additive: a house rule where new levels add to existing ones.

Players never see NPC defenses, DR, or Health in any resolution mode.

Your private notes

Every attack and save sends you a private note with the numbers players don't see. It includes buttons for:

  • Apply (with DR), No DR, and Undo for damage, all setting Health to an exact value so you can click them in any order;
  • applying or undoing condition levels;
  • the attacker's critical choice;
  • after-the-roll reactions (Block, Remaneuver, Black Rebuke …), labelled with who can use them;
  • marking an NPC Dead.

Turns

Start a combat in the Combat Tracker. Everything tied to a turn (AP refresh, condition decay, Hemorrhage, the Insane table, auras, zones, Battle Fatigue, Focus upkeep) runs on your client as the active GM. Keep one GM connected during combat.

Players roll initiative with the Initiative button on their sheets, which also adds their tokens to the combat. NPC sheets have the same button. Pressed with no combat running, it starts one on the scene you're viewing. Foundry only offers a roll to a combatant with no initiative. To roll again, use Reset Initiative in the Combat Tracker's ⋮ menu, or right-click one combatant and choose Re-roll Initiative.

NPCs

  • On an NPC sheet, Paste Stat Block fills in HP, AP, defenses, Check DC, CR, and Speed, and creates one ability for each entry you paste. An attack written as melee attack vs PD, 1d10 slashing becomes rollable; anything else stays as text for you to run.
  • NPC defenses and Max AP are typed in directly. Set the creature type so Sentinel Favored-Enemy abilities recognize it.
  • An NPC's Speed is typed in on its sheet (30ft when blank).

Adventures

The Adventures compendium holds ready-to-run adventures. Open it, then open an adventure and click Import. Its scene, actors, journals, items, and tables are added to your world in their own folders. Importing again replaces them with fresh copies.

  • The Breach is a level-5 combat one-shot for four players on Chuni's Wall. Start with its GM Guide journal, which covers setup, the four pregenerated heroes, the demons, and the battlefield. Its ballistas and oil barrels are actors every player owns, so anyone can crew them. Its pit trap is a scene Region that springs on its own.

What you adjudicate

  • Movement: any push, pull, knock-back, charge path, or "move up to your speed". The check that decides it is rolled for you; you move the tokens.
  • The battlefield: Cover, Cornered, Obscured, Shadowed, Height, and Hidden (after a successful Sneak). Toggle them on tokens; the system applies their effects.
  • Zones: moving them (drag the Region) and whether they were placed within range. You can delete a stray zone like any other Region.
  • Rend on NPCs: a monster wearing no armor can't be rended. To let Rend reach one that wears armor, give it the armor as an equipped item. Its stat-block defenses already include that armor, so only the points rended off the item come off them.
  • Anything the card marks "GM applies": Pull the Strand, and an Insane-table result chosen by Incredulous Will.

If something looks wrong

  • A number is off: every card lists the modifiers that applied and where each came from. Check the ability's dropdown settings (weapon family, chosen condition) and the token statuses (Raging, Steadied, Beast Form).
  • A turn effect didn't fire: confirm the combat has started and a GM is connected.
  • Compendium changes: after the system updates, re-drag changed abilities onto sheets. Items already on actors are copies and don't update themselves.

Glossary

  • AP: Action Points, spent on actions and refilled each turn.
  • Limbs: arm, legs, body, and mind. Reusing an exhausted limb costs +1 AP.
  • Boost: armed ahead of time; changes your next matching action.
  • Focus: lasts while you maintain it, by using its action again each turn.
  • Enduring: a condition that doesn't drop at the end of your turn.
  • Check DC: the number others roll against when you force a Trait Check.
  • Zone: a placed area (a Foundry Region) that affects creatures inside it.
